anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved: After keeps every fact Before kept. Checkpoint 1 still compares the raw `## Acceptance Criteria` bytes before the gate, shows the exact mixed `- [x]` / `2.` rows with the trailing `\n`, declares a pass, and explicitly says the bytes are locked rather than normalized; Checkpoint 2 still treats the supported scenario as a substantive full replacement with both rows normalized to `- [ ]`, the expected 12 rows retained over the observed zero, and no byte-mismatch stop; Checkpoint 3 still proposes a separate new comment carrying the original Idea verbatim while stating the older Reporter note is neither edited nor treated as satisfying the overflow. Two small things to watch so future wordings don't regress: After's Checkpoint 2 note copies row 2 (`2. Given one request...`) as displaced even though only its marker changed — keep the rule that displaced payload is text actually removed or rewritten, so the note stays verbatim-displaced rather than a second AC copy; and After's single-line `Reporter note: ...` form is fine as long as the displaced sentence itself remains byte-exact, which it does here. Otherwise the After wording delivers the Change (audit folding, byte lock for quiet repairs, full-replacement normalization, new-comment-not-mutate) without disturbing these guards.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved: After still performs an explicit AC byte check before the gate in checkpoint 1 and keeps the mixed checked/numbered rows with the trailing newline, normalizes both rows to unchecked with the expected 12 rows in the substantive checkpoint without a byte-mismatch stop, and in checkpoint 3 proposes a new verbatim ExportWrapper comment while leaving the older Reporter note untouched. Two regressions sit just outside these facts and deserve attention. First, After's checkpoints 1 and 3 inject a '+scenario: none (nothing to observe - new capability)' line into the Problem body of what the request called a prose-conformance-only repair; that is an audit field leaking into reporter prose and widens the diff beyond the single displaced sentence. The wording should say that for conformance-only repairs the body diff is limited to demoting the displaced detail, and that audit results (scenario, in-motion, sibling) are reported only on the gate's Audit line, never written into the body. Second, checkpoint 3's rewritten Idea appends a 'Pointer for the implementer' with docs/export.md#L8 and src/report-helper.ts, which is internal mechanism inside Idea and works against the bounded-prose goal; keep the attributed, product-level sketch in Idea and let the repo-fit citation live in the Audit line or the Reporter note. Before's extra '+source: https://example.test/run/R' line in checkpoint 2 was also questionable, and After correctly demotes it to a scenario input, so keep that part.
